items.note: User study (19 participants) compares the EnamelAI Painter human-GenAI porcelain-painting system with existing AI and non-AI tools; reported outcomes are creative engagement and user experience, so whether outputs were scored needs the full text; well under 50 participants.

Dissertation Study 1 is a quasi-experiment that varies LLM randomness when people write with the LLM and has evaluators rate the creativity of the work; Study 2 is AI-text detection (AI vs human DAT comparison); sample size not in the abstract.

Mainly a system evaluation of the DesignAgent LLM multi-agent tool (104 simulated sessions, model only), plus a user study against baseline systems with design accuracy and solution quality outcomes; human sample size not stated, outcome is engineering quality rather than novelty.

Field experiment with students in which questioning-enhanced GenAI raises computed fluency, flexibility, and originality of ideas; the comparison condition and sample size are not stated (ICIS 2025 proceedings, abstract from OpenAlex).

User study (24 participants) compares an LLM dynamic-graph whiteboard with a chat-only AI baseline (AI-configuration comparison) and finds higher engineering quality of final design schemes; under 50 participants.

User study (N=18) of the stickynexus sticky-note interface for GenAI-assisted design; the comparison condition is not stated and outcomes (information exploration, creative exploration) may be process or self-report measures; possibly a system paper without comparison.

Design-education workshop compares student teams using AI at the ideation stage versus the storyboarding stage (AI-configuration comparison); outcomes are the Creativity Support Index (self-report) and idea diversity of unclear measurement; abstract from the DRS landing page, no sample size.

Compares the GPSdesign GenAI problem-solution co-evolution system with a baseline system and reports greater design-space divergence and solution quality; sample size and baseline (AI or not) not stated.
CHI 2025 system paper (CoExploreDS) whose user studies report improved design quality; the comparison condition and sample size are not stated (abstract from Semantic Scholar).

First part scores AI-generated combinational ideas with and without a foundation model (model only); second part is a user study comparing the CombinatorX tool with an existing combinational creativity tool and internet search on idea-generation effectiveness; sample size not stated.
